n: Setar's product manager sold Aruba's mobile phone contracts to vendors
rank: product manager, Servicio di Telecommunicacion di Aruba (Setar)
d: Egbert Koolman was a product manager at Servicio di Telecommunicacion di Aruba, known as Setar, the island's telecommunications company, which the US Justice Department described as an instrumentality of the Aruban government. From 2005 to 2016 he took more than $1.3 million from American and other foreign vendors, and in return steered mobile phone contracts to them and handed over Setar's confidential bid information, so the companies knew what to bid and against what. He pleaded guilty on 13 April 2018 and was sentenced to 36 months and $1,308,500 in restitution. Lawrence Parker Jr., one of the vendors' side, had pleaded guilty on 28 December 2017.
inside: Foreign vendors paid a manager inside Aruba's state telecoms company for its confidential bid information, so its purchasing decisions served them.
